events_chronological: Decades ago Ingrid Ravn disappeared from the family island during a parade, on a day when a crash had blocked the only bridge.
Every year since, Gustav Ravn has received a pressed flower on his birthday, which he takes as taunting from her killer.
Journalist Anders Sten loses a libel case against the financier Kolberg and resigns from his magazine.
Sonja Vik, a ward of the state and a researcher for a security firm, is handed a new guardian, Rask, after her old one has a stroke.
Sonja compiles the background report on Sten that persuades Gustav Ravn to hire him.
Gustav brings Sten out to the island to write a family history and, in truth, to find out who killed Ingrid.
Rask makes Sonja perform oral sex before he will release her own money.
Rask rapes Sonja at his flat, not knowing she has hidden a camera in her bag.
Sonja comes back, tasers Rask, marks him permanently as a rapist and blackmails him with the recording.
Sten works through the family archive, is shot at in the woods, and finds Ingrid's notebook full of names and numbers.
Sten's daughter Maja points out that the numbers are scripture verses.
Sten asks the security firm for a research assistant and is given Sonja, who has been reading his hard drive for months.
Together they match the verses to a series of ritual murders of women across the country going back forty years.
They trace the killings to Otto Ravn, Ingrid's father, and then to her brother Viktor.
Viktor catches Sten, chains him in a soundproofed basement and explains what he does down there.
Sonja arrives, splits Viktor's face with a golf club, and lets him drive away to his death in a crash.
Sonja nurses Sten back to health and the two become lovers.
A cousin called Karin, living overseas, turns out to be Ingrid herself, using the cousin's name since fleeing her father and brother.
Ingrid comes home to Gustav, and Sten has his story.
Sonja, in disguise, empties Kolberg's accounts at a foreign bank and feeds Sten the story that destroys him, then sees him with his editor Britt and throws away the present she had bought.
nonlinear_category_reason: The investigation holds 15 of 17 scenes and runs forward, with the disappearance decades earlier reconstructed as an insertion.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs two threads in parallel for its first half - the journalist on the island and the researcher in the city - cutting between them long before they have anything to do with each other, and converging them at told-order bullet 12. Told-order bullets 4-5 are the old disappearance and the years of pressed flowers, reconstructed from photographs and testimony rather than played as present action.
fabula_notes: The disappearance and the ritual murders reaching back forty years are pieced together from documents and photographs and never dramatised as they happened, so the ordering of those events is what the investigation establishes rather than what the film shows. The researcher's own history, alluded to only as "all the evil", stays off screen.
